intended_object: Let P and P' both be localizations of R at the same submonoid S. They are canonically isomorphic as R-algebras, and this isomorphism induces a ring isomorphism between the semiring of fractional ideals of P and that of P'. The source is the docstring.
explanation:
The body uses `IsLocalization.ringEquivOfRingEquiv` with the identity on R to build the canonical isomorphism P ≃ P'. This is the unique such isomorphism compatible with the algebra maps from R. The `commutes'` field checks that it is an R-algebra isomorphism. The body then passes it to `FractionalIdeal.mapEquiv`, which turns an algebra isomorphism into a ring isomorphism on fractional ideals by taking images.

This is exactly the canonical identification described in the docstring. The setting is the right generality: any commutative ring R, any submonoid S, and any two localizations P and P'. Mathlib has no other declaration for this object.
